notes: Letter-by-letter lyrics fill the line now. A word the singer has passed keeps its letters lit, the word being sung sweeps across its own letters, and the words to come stay dark — the line fills in instead of one word flashing in place.

The sweep no longer skips words. On a line whose window was longer than the singing inside it the highlight used to jump from the first word to the last one, fully lit; every word is visited now, in order.
When the sheet moves on, the line just sung goes back to the trough, so a song cannot turn into a wall of gold by the second verse.

A Volume boost sits right under the equalizer in Settings → More. Slide it up to +15 dB — about five and a half times the signal — for a quiet master or quiet headphones. A soft ceiling catches the peaks it would otherwise clip, so it gets louder instead of crackling, and 0 dB (Off) is exactly how SideCut sounded before.
The boost is one saved number: it comes back on the next launch and applies to whatever is already playing, with no restart and no press of play.

Settings → More is six named groups now — Good to know, Sound, Playback, Library, App & data and About & updates — in one card style, with the version number, the update log, the listening streak and the version guide together in one About card instead of floating between the rollback list and the DJ card.
